newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar ends little changed.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar ends little changed.

text.p: LIFFE white sugar futures ended easier but in thin volume after trading in a range through Monday.
"It's very dull and stuck on a small range," a trader said.
Total volume on the exchange was 978 lots.
Traders said New York failed to provide the hoped-for stimulus to the London market.
In fundamental news, Bangladesh said it bought 25,000 tonnes of white sugar at $338.75 per tonne C&F from Jeddah-based Supreme Global Incorporated.
The sugar is for shipment in July-August.
Turkey's Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said the government had raised its sugar beet purchase prices 150 percent to 11,000 lira per kg from 4,400 a year earlier, Anatolian news agency reported.
Sugar beet growers had sought a rise in prices to 11,500 per kg.
Farmers had warned that if the price rise for 1997/98 was not adequate Turkey would face a shortfall and imports could follow in calendar year 1998.
